category_title: Active and physically competent children with speech and developmental delays
minimal_context: The student is playing football in the hallway with his older cousin and father.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to play football in the hallway now.

STUDENT: Play football shall we? Right chaps, run!

TUTOR: Please pass the ball to me.

STUDENT: Right. Yeah. (He verbally directs where the tutor should stand instead of passing the ball.)

TUTOR: I am standing here. Go ahead and pass it now.

STUDENT: (He ignores the instruction, concentrating fully on his own physical skills. Supremely confident in the familiar activity, he keeps the ball to himself, kicking, blocking, and tackling with skill while varying the pressure of his kicks.)

options.A: Put him in a position in the hallway where he is less distracted, so he is not seeing other things.
options.B: Playfully intervene on the ball during the game, provide a running commentary, and prompt role play.
options.C: Make sure that the cousin and father do not stop playing to gather around him and give him attention.
options.D: Elicit the student's unhelpful thought, then help him recognize how his behavior impacts the other players' willingness to accommodate his wishes.
